items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: You called me in 1943 and I was working--Johnny Littles and I were working at Sloppy Joe's, to join your band.

ctx.x: I don't know how that nickname came about.

You called me in 1943 and I was working--Johnny Littles and I were working at Sloppy Joe's, to join your band. You called me several times and I joined Basie--I was going to join you and Basie came and took me September 4, 1943.

Anyway, Bostic went on and they were all right and he came out just overnight, just saxophone fine, and then it was Freeman, a Catholic teacher--both of those boys were Catholics--and they went to the public school but they also studied Catholic and this Catholic teacher was music, and he got a little band. So they really had teaching two ways, from them, and then from the high school band too, and they kind of doubled up on things. They were very good, and Mr. Freeman was just wild about Spurgeon and Bostic.
